title: Session 5: Phrases and Clauses: Independent and Dependent
summary: The difference between a phrase and a clause, independent (IC) and dependent (DC) clauses, the three types of dependent clauses (adverb, relative, noun), and how every type of conjunction connects clauses.

blocks.title: By the end of this session you can …
items: Tell the difference between a phrase and a clause
Find the subject and verb in any clause
Identify independent and dependent clauses quickly
Recognise adverb, relative and noun clauses, and review all four types of conjunctions

rows: a group of words **without** a subject + verb pair
a group of words **with** a subject + verb
in the morning · the tall boy · after the match · to win the prize
the boy laughed · after **the match ended** · she **is** tired

blocks.title: How to find the subject and the verb
items: Find the **verb** first: the action or state word (runs, was, has finished, can swim).
Then ask **who or what** does it? That is the **subject**.
After **the match ended**, **the players** **celebrated**. → two clauses (match + ended; players + celebrated).
Careful: -ing and to + verb alone are not main verbs: running fast · to win the race are **phrases**.

blocks.title: Same words, different job
items: after the match ended → clause (subject the match + verb ended)

rows: ✓ yes — it can be a sentence
a subordinating conjunction (because, although, when, if …) or a relative word (who, which, that …)

blocks.title: The stand-alone test
items: Read the clause on its own, with a full stop. Does it sound finished? → IC.
Does it leave you waiting ("… and then what?")? → DC.
When the lights went out. → waiting → DC. The lights went out. → finished → IC.

rows: tells when, why, how, under what condition, in spite of what
subordinating conjunctions: because, although, when, if, until, since …
who, which, that, whose, where, when
The boy **who won the prize** is my cousin.
acts like a noun (subject or object)

blocks.title: Relative clauses: two points for academic writing
items: who = people · which = things · that = people or things · whose = possession · where = places.

Extra information (not needed to identify the noun) goes between commas: My brother, **who lives in Dubai**, is an engineer. Information you need goes with no commas: Students **who study every day** improve faster.

rows: either A or B · not only A but also B
IC; however, IC · IC. However, IC.

blocks.title: Count the clauses
items: Count the subject + verb pairs. That is the number of clauses.
Although **it was** cold, **we went** to the beach, and **we swam**. → 3 clauses: 1 DC + 2 ICs. (You will need this in Session 6.)

items.q: Phrase or clause? under the old bridge
Phrase or clause? when the bridge collapsed
Phrase or clause? to finish the project on time
items.a: **phrase** (to finish is not a main verb)

items.q: IC or DC? Because she was late.
items.a: **DC** — it needs an IC (fragment on its own)

items.q: IC or DC? She was late.
IC or DC? Which was the best book in the library.
Underline the subject and circle the verb: The old man in the blue coat walked slowly.
items.a: subject: The old man (in the blue coat) · verb: walked

items.q: What type of DC? The city where I was born is very old.
What type of DC? I think that you are right.
What type of DC? If you study, you will pass.
How many clauses? When the bell rang, the students packed their bags and they ran outside.
items.a: **3**: DC (the bell rang) + IC (the students packed) + IC (they ran)

items.q: Add commas: My teacher who is from Aswan speaks four languages.
items.a: My teacher, who is from Aswan, speaks four languages. (extra information)

blocks.text: Answer all 15 questions, then check your score and read the explanations. Take a screenshot of your final score and upload it to the Practice Quiz assignment on Google Classroom.

blocks.title: Session 5 Practice Quiz
blocks.intro: 15 questions. Choose the best answer. You see your score and the explanations at the end.

c: in the middle of the night

questions.q: The book **that I borrowed** was interesting. The bold part is …
I believe **that honesty is important**. The bold part is …
We stayed at home **because it was snowing**. The bold part is …
What is the subject? Every morning, the students in Year 8 run around the field.
How many clauses? The phone rang, and Nour answered it.
How many clauses? Although it was late, the shop was open, so we went in.
Which word starts a relative clause about a **person**?

c: My father who, is a doctor, works in Giza.
My father who is a doctor works in Giza.
My father, who is a doctor, works in Giza.
My father, who is a doctor works in Giza.
questions.e: Extra information about my father → commas.

questions.q: Which pair is joined by a **subordinating** conjunction?
c: Either she sang or he played.
She sang although she was tired.
She sang; however, she was tired.
